clue.text: Saint brings to church cat and a bear

parts.note: S is a short abbreviation for saint
a tom is a male cat
taken as written
CH is the usual abbreviation for church

explanation.surface: A saint arrives at church with a cat and a bear in tow, a strange menagerie for a service.
explanation.walkthrough: The saint goes first, then the cat and the 'a' are brought up to the church at the end. 'Bear' looks like the animal of the procession, but it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To stomach something is to put up with or tolerate it, which is the verb sense of bear.

clue.text: Without poles, climbing in high altitude conditions

indicators.note: in a down entry, climbing means travelling upward, so the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: W/O is the written shorthand for without
north and south are the two poles, N and S

explanation.surface: Mountaineers in thin air are managing without their walking poles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without poles' reads like climbers lacking equipment, but it is W/O followed by N and S; the whole string then climbs up the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: Snow lies on mountain peaks, so it is the typical weather and ground state found up at great heights.

clue.text: Bends down, dropping stone: my mistake

indicators.note: to drop something is to let it fall away, so part of the word is lost

parts.note: to stoop is to bend the body down
ST is the abbreviation for the stone, a British unit of weight

explanation.surface: Someone bends down and lets a stone slip, then apologises for the blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: A stone is a British weight of fourteen pounds, abbreviated ST; take those letters off the front of the bending word.
explanation.definitionFit: The exclamation is what you say on making a small blunder, an admission of an error in a single word.

clue.text: Patronage gives first-class benefits still to be received

parts.note: A is the top grade, first class

indicators.note: something received is taken in, so one piece is held inside another

parts.note: uses are benefits or advantages
a still is a single photograph, a pic

explanation.surface: A sponsorship deal provides premium perks that have not yet arrived.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Still to be received' reads as pending, but 'still' is a noun, a photograph, and 'to be received' tells the benefits to take it in.
explanation.definitionFit: Under someone's auspices means with their backing and support, so the word stands for sponsorship or protection.

clue.text: Once has to employ canine to break egg

indicators.note: a firm that employs someone takes them in, so one piece is enclosed by another

parts.note: the old form of has, as written once upon a time
C stands for a canine tooth in dental notation

explanation.surface: Someone is obliged to use a dog to crack an egg, which sounds absurd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Once' marks an archaic form of the verb. Dentists label the canine tooth C.
explanation.definitionFit: A chick hatches when it breaks out of its shell, so the verb means emerging from an egg.

clue.text: Small stroke that's hard to interpret

definitions.note: a relative clause standing for a noun: something that is hard to read

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
the crawl is a swimming stroke

explanation.surface: A tiny pen mark is so slight that nobody can make out what it means.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stroke' looks like a pen stroke, which suits the answer, but it is a swimming stroke.
explanation.definitionFit: Untidy careless handwriting is difficult to read, which is exactly what this word for messy writing describes.

clue.text: Concert at first at high volume, finally very dull

indicators.note: what comes at first is the opening letter of a word

parts.note: the opening letter of concert
high volume is loud

indicators.note: what comes finally is the closing letter of a word

parts.note: the closing letter of very

explanation.surface: A concert starts out blaring but ends up tedious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dull' seems to describe the concert's ending, but it is the definition, in the weather sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A dull sky is overcast and grey, covered by cloud, so the two adjectives match in describing weather.

clue.text: Satire's main failing: fear to introduce female

indicators.note: something failing is breaking down, so its letters fall apart and reform

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

indicators.note: to introduce something is to bring it inside, so one letter goes into another word

parts.note: alarm is sudden fear
F is the abbreviation for female

explanation.surface: A satirist's chief weakness is being too afraid to bring a woman into the story.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after the definition reads as 'is'. 'Main failing' looks like a noun phrase, but 'failing' works on 'main'.
explanation.definitionFit: Orwell's 1945 novella is a political satire on Soviet communism told through a farmyard of animals.

clue.text: Rewriting a storyline was to be expected

indicators.note: rewriting something produces a new version, so the letters are set down in a new order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A writer redrafts a plot, and that revision was always going to happen.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase is in the past tense here: 'lay' is the past of lie, so what lay in store was coming.
explanation.definitionFit: Whatever lies in store is waiting to happen in the future, so in the past it was anticipated.

clue.text: Facing work, adopt an attitude about it

parts.note: OP is short for opus, a work

indicators.note: about means around, so one word is placed round the other

parts.note: to pose is to strike an attitude
taken as written

explanation.surface: Confronted with a task, someone gets defensive and strikes a stance about it.
explanation.walkthrough: OP is the abbreviation for opus, a musical work.
explanation.definitionFit: Two things opposite each other are facing one another across a space, as in the house facing ours.

clue.text: Address of house I left Imogen's taken over

indicators.note: something taken over is absorbed into another body, so letters are swallowed inside

parts.note: HO is the abbreviation for house
Imogen is the setter, so the setter's is my
taken as written
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: The setter complains that a house she moved out of has been occupied by someone else.
explanation.walkthrough: Guardian setters often refer to themselves by name, so 'Imogen's' means MY; 'I left' are two separate pieces, not a verb phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: A homily is a sermon or moralising speech, which is a formal address delivered to an audience.

clue.text: Unreal, being first to fly over a lake

indicators.note: the first of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: the opening letter of fly
taken as written
Lake Erie is one of the North American Great Lakes

explanation.surface: Being the first person ever to fly over a lake seems too fantastic to be true.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'over' just places the first letters above the lake.
explanation.definitionFit: The archaic spelling describes the enchanted fairy world, imaginary and magical rather than existing in reality.

clue.text: Hinting madam wasted all her strength

indicators.note: something wasted is wrecked or ruined, so its letters are scattered into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A woman dropping hints has exhausted all her energy.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase usually comes as 'with might and main', so 'all her' stands in for the possessive around it.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means with every ounce of force one has, combining two old words for power and vigour.

clue.text: Gangster welcomes man of note, not one for a hot drink

indicators.note: to welcome a guest is to take them in, so one word goes inside another

parts.note: a capo is a Mafia boss

indicators.note: not means without, so the named letter is taken away

parts.note: Puccini, the Italian opera composer, a man of musical notes
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A mob boss lets in a celebrity, though not for a coffee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man of note' sounds like a famous person, but it means a composer. Remove the Roman one from the composer before the boss takes him in.
explanation.definitionFit: A cappuccino is an Italian coffee made with espresso and steamed frothy milk, served warm.

clue.text: Look up here, wandering in City Road

indicators.note: wandering means roaming without a fixed course, so the letters stray into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A tourist strolling along a London street is told to raise their eyes to the sights.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Look up' seems to mean raise your gaze, but it is looking up a word. 'In' belongs to the letters, not the link.
explanation.definitionFit: You consult a dictionary to find a word's meaning, which is what looking a word up means.

clue.text: Welcoming people came down with a roly-poly empty of nourishment

indicators.note: welcoming someone means taking them in, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: alit is a past tense of alight, to come down
men are people
taken as written

indicators.note: an emptied word has lost its contents, so only its outside letters remain

parts.note: the outside letters of roly-poly

explanation.surface: Friendly folk turned up bringing a jam roly-poly that had nothing nutritious in it.
explanation.walkthrough: A roly-poly is a British rolled suet pudding with jam. 'Welcoming' sits at the front but works on the landing verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Alimentary means relating to food and digestion, as in the alimentary canal that processes what we eat.

clue.text: Arranged to pick up computer business and failed

indicators.note: in a down entry, picking up lifts the letters so they read upward

parts.note: IT is information technology, the computer business
an engine that failed died

explanation.surface: A deal was struck to acquire a tech firm, and the venture flopped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arranged to pick up' reads like a planned collection, but 'to' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To tidy things is to put them in order, so tidied is a past-tense synonym for arranged neatly.

clue.text: Attack is in good shape

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a sudden bout or seizure, as of coughing

explanation.walkthrough: 'Attack' suggests aggression, but it is an attack of illness, a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a noun for a sudden seizure or outburst and an adjective for physical health.

clue.text: Do surveillance on second date

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for second
to date someone is to take them out

explanation.surface: A detective watches a couple on their second date.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Second date' reads as a romantic follow-up, but the ordinal is just its abbreviation and date is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Police stake out a building by watching it secretly over a period, which is keeping it under observation.

clue.text: Sink vessel, a trophy

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to send a ball into a pocket in snooker
second meaning: a container for cooking or holding things
third meaning: a cup won as a prize, informally

explanation.surface: A ship is scuttled, and with it goes the prize cup it carried.
explanation.walkthrough: Three separate meanings: 'vessel' tempts as a ship to be sunk, but it is a container.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means to pocket a snooker ball, a cooking container, and informally a sporting cup or trophy.

clue.text: Underrate Victor, wild daredevil

indicators.note: something wild is untamed and out of control, so the letters run loose into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
Victor is V in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Don't underestimate Victor, a reckless thrill-seeker.
explanation.walkthrough: Victor looks like a man's name but is the radio code word for V.
explanation.definitionFit: An adventurer seeks out risky exploits, just as a daredevil takes on dangerous stunts for excitement.

clue.text: A thousand buried — let us change physician

indicators.note: something buried is placed down inside, so one letter sits within others
to change something is to alter it, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
K stands for a thousand, as in 10K

explanation.surface: With a thousand already dead, people call for a new doctor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Let us change' sounds like a proposal, but it gives letters and an instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: The Gospel writer Luke is traditionally called the beloved physician in Paul's letter to the Colossians.

clue.text: Alter accounts of consigning literature to the flames?

definitions.note: a gerund phrase, while the answer is a verb phrase
definitions.meaning: second meaning, playful: literally putting volumes over the heat

explanation.surface: Someone describes fraudulent bookkeeping as like a book burning.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the second meaning as a literal, jokey reading of the idiom.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to falsify financial records, and read literally it describes putting volumes over a fire.

clue.text: For a long time congregation understood nothing

parts.note: O looks like zero, nothing
a fold is a flock, a church's congregation
read as under-stood: the next piece stands below the one before it in this down entry

explanation.surface: For years the churchgoers grasped none of the preaching.
explanation.walkthrough: Split 'understood' as under-stood: in a down entry the congregation stood under nothing, so the zero goes on top.
explanation.definitionFit: Of old means in times long past, a phrase for something going back many years.

clue.text: Examination of insurance company that sacked head

indicators.note: sacking the head removes the leader, so the opening letter is dropped

parts.note: Aviva is a large British insurance company

explanation.surface: An inquiry is held into an insurer that fired its chief executive.
explanation.walkthrough: Aviva is a big UK insurer; dropping its first letter leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A viva is an oral examination, especially the spoken defence of a university thesis.

clue.text: Like creating, ignoring the boundaries

indicators.note: ignoring a word's boundaries means leaving off its edge letters at each end

parts.note: creating is making

explanation.surface: Being creative is about refusing to stay within the lines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Like' starts the clue as if comparing, and it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Akin means similar or related to, so something akin to another is much like it.

clue.text: Leaderless priest from America who took the plunge

indicators.note: without a leader means the first letter is removed

parts.note: a vicar is a parish priest
US is America

explanation.surface: A US clergyman with no boss made a bold decision.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Took the plunge' reads as a brave choice, but here it is a literal fall from the sky.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the boy flew too near the sun on wax wings and fell into the sea.

clue.text: US singer died, over in a flash

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so letters are set within another word

parts.note: a blink is a flash, a very short moment
OB is short for obiit, Latin for died
O is the cricket abbreviation for an over

explanation.surface: An American pop star died, and it was all finished in an instant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'US singer' suggests a pop star but means a bird. OB marks a death date on gravestones; an over is six balls in cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: The bobolink is a North American songbird, so a singer native to the United States.

clue.text: Melon cut with axes: that's inspired

indicators.note: a thing cut with something has that thing driven into it, so letters go inside

parts.note: an ogen is a variety of small sweet melon
x and y are the axes of a graph

explanation.surface: Someone hacks a melon apart with hatchets and calls it a brilliant idea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Axes' suggests choppers, but it is the plural of axis.
explanation.definitionFit: To inspire is literally to breathe in, and oxygen is the gas we take into our lungs.

clue.text: Step on to platform and run into arrest

indicators.note: into means going inside, so one letter enters another word

parts.note: to detain is to arrest
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A fugitive gets off at the station and runs straight into the police.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Step on to platform' sounds like boarding or getting on a stage, but it means getting off at a station.
explanation.definitionFit: To detrain is to alight from a railway carriage, which puts the passenger onto the station platform.
